title: Fazola's tone and the Prima Little Club photograph
summary: Fazola's cool tone, personnel in a 1930 Prima band photo, Meyer Weinberg.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: How was Vazola's tone on the sax? The sax, fine.
He had a good, he had a cool tone. But that clad was the best tone. He used a stiff read to him on a three and a half.

Well, you see, I never heard him play sax, really, except maybe in the section. Here's this band at the Little Club. Prima Chalkman, the orchestra, 1930. With Charlie Hawkman on the trombone. Oh yeah, Charlie Hawkman was a good band. I told him on that. Chalky Leon, Prima, Foss, Winstyn, Unifacon. Yeah, what's his setup? Same setup, Schilling. Yeah, same setup, Louis Macenton too, but I had Sussaphone. Yeah, he was a single, but he also played string bass too. Yeah, and Freddie Locano's got a banjo in the picture. Yeah. And Frank Benares at the piano. Yeah, that's right. Same band, just a band. Same band. I think it was a same band. Exactly. But somebody came in on sax too. Maya Weinberg. Yeah, what did he play, tenor or alto? Alto. Alto.
Alto and Clarinet. He played a fine clarinet.
And what happened to him? I don't know. He was almost...
I attacked him. He was playing with, uh... I wasn't even a good while back before he became famous. Louis Prima, a lot of times, used to make a lot of records.
